section_summary: This section (pages 95–174) contains U.S. State Department correspondence, diplomatic despatches, telegrams, and cross-reference sheets from June through September 1932 documenting the proceedings and legislative outcomes of the 62nd and 63rd extraordinary sessions of the Japanese Imperial Diet. The materials focus heavily on Japan's foreign policy under the national coalition cabinet of Prime Minister Viscount Makoto Saito, prominently featuring major policy addresses by Premier Saito and Foreign Minister Count Kosai Uchida regarding the impending diplomatic recognition of Manchukuo, relations with China, the League of Nations, and the Nine-Power Treaty. Significant coverage is also devoted to parliamentary debates and emergency legislative measures addressing severe domestic agrarian distress, industrial depression, exchange depreciation, financial debt relief, and the political reverberations of the May 15, 1932 assassination of Prime Minister Tsuyoshi Inukai.

subfiles.about: Telegram reporting a Reuter dispatch from Nanking on the Chinese Foreign Office spokesman's response to Viscount Saito's Diet address.
subfiles.summary: American Minister Nelson T. Johnson transmits a June 5 Reuter dispatch from Nanking regarding statements by a Chinese Foreign Office spokesman. The spokesman disputed Viscount Saito's claims concerning troop movements, asserting that the Shanghai agreement does not limit Chinese troop movements within Chinese territory and placing blame for the Shanghai incident on Japanese aggression. He affirmed China's willingness to attend a round-table conference if modeled after the Washington Conference to settle Sino-Japanese issues comprehensively, while noting that open Japanese support for Manchukuo intensified Chinese suspicions of Japanese sincerity.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 618 from Peiping Transmitting Chinese Foreign Office Reaction to Viscount Saito's Speech

subfiles.about: Document file note referencing Peiping telegram No. 608 regarding Viscount Saito's address before the Diet.
subfiles.summary: This State Department document file note cross-references telegram No. 608 of June 4, 1932, from Johnson in China to decimal file 894.00/411, filed under 894.032/106. It indicates that the telegram transmits press quotations of Viscount Saito's address before the Diet dealing with the feeling of insecurity and unrest in Japan.
subfiles.title: Document File Note for Peiping Telegram No. 608

subfiles.about: Telegram transmitting a Reuter report on Admiral Viscount Saito's statement of government policy in the Diet on June 3, 1932.
subfiles.summary: Minister Johnson reports a Reuter dispatch from Tokyo summarizing the policy address delivered by Premier Admiral Viscount Saito to the Diet. Saito emphasized the urgent necessity of dispelling social insecurity and guaranteeing livelihood stability amid acute economic depression, rural misery, and urban unemployment. He pledged to purify politics, seek support equally from the two major political parties without favoring either, and fulfill public aspirations for political reform.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 608 from Peiping Transmitting Reuter Report on Premier Saito's Policy Speech

subfiles.about: Document file note referencing a State Department memorandum on the advance copy of the Japanese Foreign Minister's Diet speech.
subfiles.summary: This State Department document file note (894.032/107) cross-references a memorandum dated June 2, 1932, filed under 793.94/5296. It records that a copy of the speech to be delivered by the Japanese Minister for Foreign Affairs at the opening of the Diet concerning foreign relations was handed to Secretary Stimson by the Japanese Ambassador.
subfiles.title: Document File Note for Memorandum on Japanese Foreign Minister's Diet Speech

subfiles.about: Official English text of the address delivered by Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Viscount Makoto Saito at the opening of the Diet.
subfiles.summary: Viscount Saito reviews Japan's foreign relations, beginning with the cessation of hostilities at Shanghai, the planned withdrawal of Japanese military forces, and hopes for a permanent peace conference. He turns to Manchuria, asserting that Manchukuo's existence cannot be ignored in future international adjustments, while justifying Japanese military operations against bandits and repudiating rumors of impending war with the Soviet Union. Saito further reports on Japan's cooperation with the League of Nations inquiry commission, its participation in the Geneva Disarmament Conference, and the conclusion of new commercial treaties with Portugal and French Indochina.
subfiles.title: Address of the Minister for Foreign Affairs of Japan, Viscount Makoto Saito, at the Opening of the Diet

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum summarizing Tokyo Despatch No. 30 on the proceedings and legislation of the 62nd Diet session.
subfiles.summary: Salisbury summarizes Tokyo Despatch No. 30 describing the 62nd session of the Diet held from June 1 to June 15, 1932, noting the remarkable decorum of the proceedings and the passage of 19 government bills. He highlights speeches by a proletarian representative criticizing military influence over the cabinet and insinuating War Office collusion in Premier Inukai's assassination. The memorandum also summarizes Premier Saito's remarks on financial distress, rural relief, the eventual recognition of Manchukuo, adherence to the Open Door, and proposed study of Nine-Power Treaty revision.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Tokyo Despatch No. 30 Regarding the 62nd Diet

subfiles.about: Embassy despatch reviewing the proceedings of the 62nd Diet and enclosing excerpts of parliamentary debates on Manchukuo and foreign policy.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew provides a comprehensive report on the 62nd extraordinary Diet session, detailing nineteen enacted measures covering loan flotations for Manchurian military operations, general budget deficits, Bank of Japan note issuance, exchange control, and silk stabilization. The despatch notes the parties' desire to avoid partisan squabbling, proletarian delegate Sugiyama's fiery attack on military interference, and interpellations directed at War Minister Araki concerning the May 15 assassination of Premier Inukai. Enclosed translations document extensive interpellations by Yosuke Matsuoka, Baron Ida, Baron Kusuda, and Mr. Kodama regarding the recognition of Manchukuo, potential withdrawal from the League of Nations, the Open Door principle, and the Nine-Power Treaty.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 30: Proceedings of the 62nd Diet, with Enclosures

subfiles.about: Document file note referencing Tokyo Despatch No. 38 regarding the convening, adjournment, and legislation of the 62nd Diet.
subfiles.summary: This State Department document file note cross-references Tokyo Despatch No. 38 (filed under 894.00 P.R./55) dated July 1, 1932, from Ambassador Grew. It indicates that the despatch reports on the convening and adjournment of the 62nd session of the Imperial Diet and the bills passed during its sittings.
subfiles.title: Document File Note for Tokyo Despatch No. 38 (Political Report No. 55)

subfiles.about: Telegram reporting that Foreign Minister Count Uchida's forthcoming Diet speech will be telegraphed directly to Washington for release.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew informs the Department of State that the Japanese Foreign Office will cable an advance 2,000-word text of Count Uchida's upcoming Diet speech to the Japanese Embassies in Washington and London for simultaneous press release. Grew notes that since the text will be readily accessible in Washington, he will not cable its substance unless specifically instructed.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 218 from Tokyo Regarding Count Uchida's Forthcoming Diet Speech

subfiles.about: Telegram transmitting a Reuter report on anticipated Diet speeches by Uchida, Saito, and Takahashi, and rumors concerning Manchukuo recognition.
subfiles.summary: Minister Johnson forwards a Reuter report from Tokyo detailing public eagerness for ministerial policy addresses by Count Uchida, Viscount Saito, and Finance Minister Takahashi. The report notes that Uchida's speech will focus strictly on China and Manchukuo, and reviews differing forecasts concerning the formal recognition of Manchukuo, expected after General Muto visits Changchun and the Privy Council deliberates.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1006 from Peiping Transmitting Reuter Report on Diet Speeches and Manchukuo Recognition

subfiles.about: Excerpt from Tokyo Despatch No. 38 noting the formal opening and adjournment dates of the 62nd extraordinary Diet.
subfiles.summary: This extracted section from Tokyo Despatch No. 38 (Political Report No. 55) records that the sixty-second extraordinary session of the Diet opened on June 1 in the presence of the Emperor. It notes that the session adjourned on June 14 (or 15) following Premier Viscount Saito's reading of the Imperial rescript.
subfiles.title: Extract from Tokyo Despatch No. 38 (Political Report No. 55) on the 62nd Session of the Diet

subfiles.about: Telegram reporting unanimous Japanese press approval of Foreign Minister Count Uchida's Diet speech on Manchuria.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew reports that Japanese newspapers without exception expressed hearty approval of Count Uchida's August 25 speech before the Diet. The press warmly endorsed his declaration that Japan would recognize Manchukuo based on solid realities rather than abstract theories, praising the address as a bold and decisive departure from previous timid diplomacy.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 221 from Tokyo Regarding Japanese Press Reception of Count Uchida's Speech

subfiles.about: Document file note referencing Peiping telegram No. 1012 regarding press commentary on Count Uchida's Diet speech.
subfiles.summary: This State Department document file note cross-references Peiping telegram No. 1012 of August 26, 1932, originally filed under 893.01-Manchuria/405 and placed under 894.032/114. It indicates that the telegram reports on press commentary regarding Count Uchida's speech before the Japanese Diet.
subfiles.title: Document File Note for Peiping Telegram No. 1012

subfiles.about: Telegram transmitting an editorial from the North China Daily News criticizing Foreign Minister Count Uchida's Diet address.
subfiles.summary: Minister Johnson transmits a Shanghai Reuter report quoting an editorial from the North China Daily News on Count Uchida's Diet address. The editorial disputes that Japan's intervention and the creation of Manchukuo reflected the will of the local population, challenging Uchida's optimistic portrayal of conditions in the new state. It sharply criticizes Uchida for subordinating international agreements and sanctity of pledges to unilateral national interests, and for abandoning collective peace efforts in favor of military force.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1012 from Peiping Transmitting North China Daily News Editorial on Count Uchida's Speech

subfiles.about: Document file note referencing Peiping telegram No. 1023 regarding speeches delivered by Count Uchida in the Diet.
subfiles.summary: This State Department document file note cross-references Peiping telegram No. 1023 of August 29, 1932, filed under 894.00/430 and decimal 894.032/115. It records that the telegram transmits reporting on speeches delivered by Japanese Foreign Minister Count Uchida in the Imperial Diet.
subfiles.title: Document File Note for Peiping Telegram No. 1023

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum summarizing Tokyo Despatch No. 110 on the first five days of the 63rd Diet session.
subfiles.summary: Salisbury provides a detailed summary of Tokyo Despatch No. 110, which reviews the initial five days of the 63rd extraordinary Diet. The memorandum outlines Kaku Mori's 'Back to Asia' interpellation urging Japan to sever ties with decadent Western civilization, Finance Minister Takahashi's testimony on the seven-billion-yen national debt and gold embargo, inquiries into Inukai's assassination, and Seigo Nakano's denunciation of Secretary Stimson's August 8 address. It also notes slight textual variations between the Foreign Office's English translation of Uchida's speech and the copy provided by the Japanese Embassy in Washington.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Tokyo Despatch No. 110 Regarding the 63rd Diet

subfiles.about: Embassy despatch providing a day-by-day record of the 63rd Diet from August 22 to 26 and enclosing the full text of Count Uchida's address.
subfiles.summary: First Secretary Dickover submits a day-by-day account of the 63rd extraordinary Diet summoned to enact emergency relief legislation. The despatch describes the opening ceremonies, ministerial statements by Premier Saito and Finance Minister Takahashi, and significant interpellations, including Kaku Mori's advocacy of an Asian-centric policy and Seigo Nakano's sharp rebuke of U.S. Secretary Stimson. Transmitted with the despatch is the complete official English translation of Foreign Minister Count Uchida's August 25 address, which asserts that recognizing Manchukuo is essential to Far Eastern peace, defends Japanese actions under the right of self-defense, denies violations of the Nine-Power Treaty or Kellogg-Briand Pact, and firmly rejects any restoration of Chinese control over Manchuria.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 110: Day-by-day Résumé of the 63rd Diet, with Enclosure of Count Uchida's Address

subfiles.about: Document file note referencing London Despatch No. 333 transmitting British editorial commentary on Count Uchida's Diet speech.
subfiles.summary: This State Department document file note cross-references London Despatch No. 333 of September 2, 1932, from Chargé d'Affaires Ray Atherton, filed under 893.01-Manchuria/445 and placed under 894.032/117. It indicates that the despatch transmits English press editorial commentary regarding Count Uchida's speech before the Diet.
subfiles.title: Document File Note for London Despatch No. 333

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum summarizing Tokyo Despatch No. 115 on the final seven days of the 63rd Diet session.
subfiles.summary: Salisbury summarizes Tokyo Despatch No. 115 detailing the last seven days of the 63rd Diet. The memorandum notes Finance Minister Takahashi's mention of a secret 'stratagem' for loan redemption, his warnings against artificial yen control, and a closed Peers session investigating Prime Minister Inukai's assassination. It also highlights Foreign Minister Uchida's readiness to face adverse League votes and War Minister Araki's remarks on military readiness and the complex international considerations surrounding military operations toward Jehol.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Tokyo Despatch No. 115 Regarding the 63rd Diet

subfiles.about: Embassy despatch presenting a day-by-day account of the 63rd Diet from August 27 to September 4, 1932, and cataloging enacted legislation.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew chronicles the contentious final days of the 63rd Diet, which required two extensions before concluding on September 4. The report traces heated clashes between the cabinet and the Seiyukai over the Rice and Cereals Law and agrarian debt adjustment, resulting in the passage of the government's rice bill, the shelving of the agrarian debt bill, and the approval of a modified debt mediation measure. The despatch also details debates on currency decline, a secret hearing on Inukai's assassination, War Minister Araki's statements on military readiness regarding Jehol, and provides an itemized summary of all sixteen enacted bills.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 115: Day-by-day Résumé of the 63rd Diet (August 27 - September 4, 1932)

subfiles.about: Document file note referencing Tokyo Political Report No. 57 concerning the opening proceedings of the 63rd Diet.
subfiles.summary: This State Department document file note cross-references a Tokyo Despatch dated September 1, 1932 (Political Report No. 57, filed under 894.00-P.R./57). It notes that the report treats the 63rd session of the Japanese Imperial Diet and indicates that no important legislation was enacted during the opening days of August.
subfiles.title: Document File Note for Tokyo Despatch (Political Report No. 57)

subfiles.about: Excerpt from page 25 of Tokyo Political Report No. 57 detailing the convocation and early debates of the 63rd Diet session.
subfiles.summary: This extract from Political Report No. 57 describes the convocation of the 63rd extraordinary session of the Diet on August 22, 1932, convened pursuant to an Imperial rescript to address emergency economic relief. It recounts that strong opposition from the Seiyukai and the National League over the budget, the Rice and Cereals Law, and agricultural debt adjustment necessitated extensions beyond the original nine-day schedule. The report concludes by noting that the full proceedings of the session are detailed in Embassy Despatch No. 110.
subfiles.title: Extract from Tokyo Despatch (Political Report No. 57) on the Course of Legislation in the 63rd Diet
